ai.title: Add NEXTPUBLICBACKENDURL to env schema
ai.summary: Added `NEXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL` to the client-side environment validation in `env.ts`. This ensures the backend URL is explicitly required and validated for the npm-app. The `package.json` for `npm-app` also received a new `start-js` script to build and run the JavaScript output.

eli5.text: The program now checks that a backend server address is provided and properly formatted before it starts, so it will refuse to run if that address is missing or invalid. The package for the npm app also gained a shortcut to build and start the app using pre-built JavaScript files. You would notice this if the app suddenly fails to start until you add the required server address to its settings. This is live now for anyone running the npm app.

ai.title: start-js script updated to include clean-package step
ai.summary: The `start-js` script in `npm-app/package.json` now executes `bun run clean-package.js` after building. This step was missing, causing stale artifacts to persist during the transition to the JavaScript entrypoint. The change ensures a clean state before `node` launches `dist/index.js` via `tsconfig-paths`. Scope limited to `npm-app` build scripts.

eli5.text: When you start your app in development using the JavaScript version of the start command, the tool that runs it now does one extra cleanup step first. Without that step, old build files were sticking around and could get mixed in with the new ones, so your app might have run on a mix of yesterday's and today's code. The cleanup now runs automatically before the app launches, so you always start from a fresh, clean state. This only affects the team members who launch the app this way, and it happens every time you use that start command.

eli5.text: The build for the assistant's npm package was reordered so the step that fixes file references now runs after the shared code libraries are copied in, preventing broken links in the final bundle. The tool that performs this reference fixing was also added to the project's dependency list so the build can find it automatically. If you looked at the build output today, you would see the steps listed in a different order and the reference-fixing tool running later, after the shared code folders are in place.

eli5.text: The automated system that builds the project's code was failing because a helper tool used the newest version of a package it depends on, which turned out to be incompatible with the project's setup. Engineers fixed this by telling the system to use an older, known-good version of that helper tool instead. This only affects the team's internal build process and has no impact on the software you use today.

ai.title: Bump version to 1.0.323
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.323 in npm-app/package.json. Updates package metadata for release.

eli5.text: Your assistant just got a new release that switches the default AI model to Gemini 2.5 Pro for regular tasks while keeping a more experimental model for special agent modes, so you'll automatically get the stronger model for everyday help. The update also adds the ability to give the AI a thinking budget, basically how much time and effort it spends reasoning before answering, so trickier tasks can get more of that reasoning time. Behind the scenes, the system got better at deciding when a task is going in circles and should stop, and it fixed a few bugs around how it cleans up messy formatting when showing code changes to you. This release is live today for anyone using the agent modes, and the new model will be used automatically without you needing to change any settings.

ai.title: web: start bypasses Nx
ai.summary: web/package.json start and discord:start scripts now invoke next start and bun run scripts/discord/index.ts directly. web/project.json start and discord:start executors removed. Eliminates Nx indirection for local web and discord service startup.

eli5.text: When you want to see the website or the Discord helper running locally, the two startup commands now fire up directly instead of going through a middleman tool first. If you tried to start things up, you'd notice the commands respond immediately without the extra layer of coordination that used to step in between. The underlying tool that coordinated these tasks still exists for other jobs, but it no longer sits in the way of these two particular startup paths.

ai.title: Parallel research tool spawns read-only sub-agents before planning
ai.summary: Adds a `research` tool that accepts a JSON array of prompts to run parallel information-gathering tasks. Each sub-agent uses `loopMainPrompt` in `lite` mode with `readOnlyMode: true`, suppressing analytics and restricting to read-only tools. `main-prompt.ts` now uses a `MainPromptOptions` object; ASK-mode instructions direct agents to use `research` instead of answering directly. `create_plan` instructions mandate running `research` first. `end_turn` removed from `TOOLS_WHICH_END_THE_RESPONSE` in favor of `research`.

eli5.text: You can now ask the assistant to investigate multiple questions or topics at the same time instead of waiting for answers one by one. When you request this, the assistant spins off several small helper agents that gather information in parallel. Each helper stays in read-only mode, meaning it only looks things up and gathers facts without changing anything, and it runs with lighter, analytics-free settings. Once all the helpers finish their research, the assistant collects and presents what each one found, then uses that combined information to form its final response or plan.

eli5.text: The system that checks a special web address used by the app's helper tools used to demand that the address look exactly like a complete website link (like https://something.com). Now it only asks that the address not be empty. This matters for people who set up or run these helper tools, if your address didn't look like a standard website, the system would reject it before; now a wider range of valid addresses will be accepted. The change is already live.

eli5.text: The assistant gained a new tool that can send several research questions out at once and collect answers in parallel, so multi-part research tasks finish faster. It also gained a web-focused start command that skips the usual project build steps, letting web work begin without waiting on the full project pipeline. A previously strict check on the backend URL setting was loosened, so the app now accepts a wider range of URL formats in that environment variable. These changes are all live today in version 1.0.324.

Admin org routes force dynamic rendering with export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'. Feed API Substack schema allows nullable cover_image. eli5.text: If you've noticed the internal admin tools loading slowly or the feed export page stalling, that should be ironed out now: the build system now converts all configuration values into consistent text automatically instead of manually handling the port number, and the admin organization export routes always generate fresh data on each request rather than reusing cached results. The feed endpoint also stops breaking when a Substack post is missing its cover image. These fixes apply only to staff and internal admin users of the private control panel and are already live.

ai.title: Sonnet restored as default agent model; Gemini moved to experimental
ai.summary: Agent mode defaults for normal and max cost settings revert to Sonnet, while Gemini 2.5 Pro Preview shifts to experimental. This adjustment in common/src/constants.ts prioritizes Sonnet for standard agent operations. The change affects core model resolution logic for agent tasks.

eli5.text: If you use this tool in agent mode, the assistant now defaults back to using the Sonnet model for everyday and high-cost tasks, while the Gemini 2.5 Pro Preview model has been moved behind an experimental setting you'd have to opt into. This swap happened in the core configuration that decides which AI model gets pulled for agent work, and it rolls back a prior decision to make Gemini the default. You'd notice this if you're regularly chatting with the assistant, since the responses would come from a different underlying model than they did just before this change.

ai.title: Remove unused @/env path mapping from tsconfig.base.json
ai.summary: Removed the `@/env` path mapping from `tsconfig.base.json`. This cleanup eliminates an unused alias that pointed to a non-existent or unimported `./env.ts` file. The change affects the base TypeScript configuration used across the repo, ensuring path aliases reflect actual imports. No runtime behavior changes.

eli5.text: The team cleaned up a leftover shortcut in the project settings that pointed to a file nobody was using. No one's experience changes as a result, since that shortcut wasn't referenced anywhere; the project simply has one fewer dead link in its configuration today.

ai.title: Add git eval leaderboard
ai.summary: Added `git_eval_results` table via migration `0020_young_sleeper.sql` to store git evaluation metrics. Includes new API route `web/src/app/api/git-evals/route.ts` and UI page `web/src/app/evals/page.tsx` for displaying results. Eval runner scripts `evals/git-evals/run-git-evals.ts` and `run-eval-set.ts` handle execution and data population.

eli5.text: The system now keeps a permanent record of how well it performs when editing real-world codebases, like a report card that shows up in a new leaderboard view. Every time the team runs a batch of automated coding tests, the results, such as accuracy, cost, and which AI models were used, get saved into a new database table and displayed on a public page, so you can compare performance across different models and repositories. This makes the evaluation data visible and trackable starting today.

ai.title: Fix AI SDK error serialization
ai.summary: ai-sdk.ts now stringifies object errors via JSON.stringify instead of casting to string. Prevents '[object Object]' in thrown exceptions. Internal fix in vercel-ai-sdk stream handler.

eli5.text: When the assistant hit a problem behind the scenes, the error message it showed was just the meaningless text 'object Object' instead of the real reason. Now it writes out the full details of the problem in plain text, so anyone looking at the logs or the failed response can see what actually went wrong. This only affects what developers see while building and testing; it does not change how the assistant answers you.

ai.title: Add Evals GitHub Actions workflow
ai.summary: New `.github/workflows/evals.yml` triggers `bun run --cwd evals run-eval-set` on pushes containing `[buffbench]` in commit message. Uses `oven-sh/setup-bun@v2` (1.2.12) and `actions/cache@v3` for `node_modules`. Injects secrets via `scripts/generate-ci-env.js` and `jq`, setting `CODEBUFF_GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT=test`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_INFISICAL_UP=true`, and `CODEBUFF_GITHUB_TOKEN`.

eli5.text: The development team has set up an automatic system that will run quality-checking tests on their software whenever someone commits code with a special tag in the message. These tests, which verify the assistant's responses against certain criteria, will only trigger for internal commits marked with a specific keyword, so they won't run during normal development work. If you were watching the build system, you'd see a new automated job start up whenever someone pushes code with that tag, running tests to ensure the AI behaves correctly.

ai.title: Add 6 hour timeout to evals CI workflow
ai.summary: Added `timeout-minutes: 360` to the `run-evals` job in `.github/workflows/evals.yml`. This enforces a 6-hour limit on evaluation runs triggered by commits containing `[buffbench]`. The change applies only to the CI workflow configuration.

eli5.text: The automated evaluation tests that run for the internal BuffBench tool now automatically stop if they run for more than six hours, preventing them from hanging indefinitely. This only affects internal engineers running these specific tests, not end users. If you triggered one of these test runs and it was taking unusually long, it will now cut off on its own after the six-hour mark rather than continuing forever.

ai.title: Parallel git evals via child process fork
ai.summary: Git evals now run in parallel by forking child processes via `run-single-eval-process.ts` instead of sequential execution. `setupTestRepo` isolates checkouts per commit SHA and skips re-cloning if the directory exists. `run-eval-set.ts` uncomments the 'manifold' eval and removes the 'codebuff' limit. Internal test infrastructure change; no user-facing impact.

eli5.text: The system that checks how well the assistant performs on coding tasks now runs those checks in parallel instead of one after another. Instead of waiting for each repository test to finish before starting the next, the system splits the work across multiple processes that run at the same time. This change only affects the internal team that evaluates the assistant's performance; you wouldn't notice it in your daily use.

ai.title: Parallelize git evals
ai.summary: Refactored `run-eval-set.ts` to execute git evaluations in parallel using `Promise.allSettled` instead of sequential loops. Updated `run-git-evals.ts` to improve log naming by sanitizing commit messages and including repo names in log directories. CI timeout for evals reduced from 360 to 180 minutes in `.github/workflows/evals.yml` to accommodate parallel execution speedups.

eli5.text: The team that runs automated coding tests made those tests run side by side instead of one after another, so the whole batch finishes faster. The test logs now get clearer names that include which code project they came from and cleaner version of the commit message. You would notice this only if you dig into the testing logs used by engineers; the time limit the tests are allowed to run before being canceled was also halved, which is now safe because they finish sooner.

ai.title: Remove partial json save in git evals
ai.summary: Removes partial JSON result saving logic from run-git-evals.ts. Eliminates intermediate file writes during evaluation runs. Updates run-eval-set.ts to restore email sending flag and remove hardcoded limits.

eli5.text: The system stopped saving incomplete test results to your computer during git evaluation runs. Previously, it would write a partial file every time a test finished so you could see progress, but those intermediate saves are no longer being made. The final results are still produced correctly; you just won't see them appear gradually as the run goes on. This only affects the internal evaluation tooling used by developers, so most users won’t notice anything at all.
